questions.question: How can a music generation system be guided to keep an existing tune while changing instrumentation or style?
options: Condition it on a melody representation such as a chromagram
Only increase the sample rate to 48 kHz
Convert the song into speaker embeddings
Use speaker diarization before decoding
questions.explanation: The lesson discusses melody-conditioned generation as a way to preserve tune while changing timbre. It specifically mentions chromagram-style conditioning for prompts like turning a melody into a string quartet.

questions.question: Why is generating a full song with lyrics generally harder than generating a short instrumental clip?
options: Songs require long-range structure plus vocal and lyric coherence
Instrumentals need more GPU memory than songs
Lyrics remove the need for conditioning
Short clips cannot be generated autoregressively
questions.explanation: The lesson separates instrumental generation from full-song generation because songs add more constraints than just local audio quality. A model has to maintain structure over time while also handling vocals, lyrics, and phrasing coherently.

questions.question: What does FAD measure in the lesson?
options: How well vocals stay on pitch in generated songs
Fréchet distance between embedding distributions of real and generated audio
The exact BPM drift over a 4-minute track
The copyright risk score of a prompt
questions.explanation: The lesson defines FAD as Fréchet Audio Distance computed in an embedding space such as VGGish or PANNs. It is useful for distribution-level regression testing, though the lesson also says it is not a replacement for human listening.

questions.question: Which model is described as the open community's closest thing to Suno for full-song lyric-conditioned generation?
options: Stable Audio Open
ACE-Step XL
MusicGen-small
AudioLDM2
questions.explanation: The lesson says ACE-Step, especially the 4B XL release, extends codec-token generation toward full songs with lyrics. It explicitly calls it the open community's closest thing to Suno.

questions.question: What safe-to-ship pattern does the lesson recommend for avoiding commercial-vocal licensing baggage with open models?
options: Always prompt for celebrity style and filter later
Generate only 4-minute songs with vocals
Skip disclosure metadata if the model is open source
Generate instrumental-only music with tools like MusicGen or Stable Audio Open
questions.explanation: In the legal section, the lesson lists instrumental-only generation as one of the safest shipping patterns. It contrasts that with commercial vocal generation, which carries more licensing and compliance complications.
